newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah satisfied with south Lebanon peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah satisfied with south Lebanon peace deal.

text.p: The pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Friday a U.S.-brokered deal that halted Israel's 17-day blitz of Lebanon a year ago has sharply reduced civilian casualties in the guerrilla war in south Lebanon.

Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah, Hizbollah's secretary-general, told a news conference on the first anniversary of the start of Israel's April 11-27 "Grapes of Wrath" blitz that three Lebanese civilians had been killed in the past year.
"Only three civilians were killed by Israel's aggressive actions since the understanding was reached, but 23 civilians were killed in the same period of the previous year," he said.
"The April understanding secured safety for our people in villages on the confrontation lines," he added.

Hizbollah has also refrained, in line with the ceasefire understanding, from firing Katyusha rockets into Israel since the Israeli bombardment ended but Nasrallah hinted that Katyushas could fly again.

He said Israel had recently committed many breaches of the ceasefire to which Hizbollah had not retaliated. "We preserve our right to retaliate for the Israeli breaches in the time that we decide," he added.
Nasrallah's news conference was the only event held in Lebanon on Friday marking the start of the blitz, which killed 200 people, mainly civilians and caused damage estimated at $500 million.

However, official ceremonies will be held on the April 18 anniversary of the "Massacre at Qana" in which about 100 civilians were killed when Israel shelled a U.N. peacekeepers' base at the southern town of Qana in which 800 refugees were sheltering.
Israel launched the blitz saying it was to destroy Hizbollah and stop it firing Katyushas at northern Israel.
Hizbollah, which said it only bombarded Israel in reply to shelling of Lebanese villages, emerged almost intact from the confrontation and continued firing Katyushas throughout the bombardment.
"The aggression was a complete failure, the Islamic resistance won a complete victory with its military and organizational force safe," Nasrallah told the news conference.

The April 26 understanding which ended the blitz banned shooting from or at civilian areas in Israel's war in south Lebanon with Hizbollah guerrillas who are trying to drive its troops from the country.
It set up a five-nation monitoring group to examine complaints about breaches of the ceasefire to avert future escalations. The group includes the United States, France, Israel, Syria and Lebanon.
